record.issuing_body: Nebraska Legislature (LB 525 introduced by Sen. Mike Jacobson on behalf of Gov. Jim Pillen; AI provisions from LB 1185 by Sen. Eliot Bostar)
record.official_identifier: LB 525 (Nebraska Legislature, 2026), incorporating LB 1185 (Conversational Artificial Intelligence Safety Act)
record.summary: Adopts the Conversational Artificial Intelligence Safety Act. Operators of conversational AI services must disclose that the user is interacting with AI whenever a user reasonably could believe they are interacting with a human being, and must apply additional safeguards for minor account holders. Operators must keep a protocol for responding to prompts involving suicidal ideation or self-harm that includes referral to crisis services, and a service may not claim to be designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care. The Attorney General enforces the provisions through civil actions.
record.notes: LB 525, introduced in the 2025 session by Sen. Mike Jacobson on behalf of Gov. Jim Pillen, mainly protects agricultural data: controllers of such data need written consent agreements with agricultural producers, and from 1 Jan 2027 every new contract on agricultural data must prohibit its sale without the producer's express written consent. The provisions of LB 1185 (Sen. Eliot Bostar), which adopt the Conversational Artificial Intelligence Safety Act, were added to it, and the combined bill passed 49-0.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026: re-read the Nebraska Legislature's Unicameral Update session review of the Banking, Commerce and Insurance Committee (15 May 2026), stored again from update.legislature.ne.gov on 17 Oct 2026 (only the site's sidebar changed since 11 Oct 2026). It confirms the act's name, the incorporation of LB 1185 into LB 525, the sponsors, the provisions in the summary, enforcement by the Attorney General and the 49-0 vote. It does not say when the Governor signed the bill or when the AI provisions become operative: date_published (14 Apr 2026) and date_in_force (1 Jul 2027) rest on version 1, which took them from law-firm summaries and LegiScan excerpts without storing them. The slip law on nebraskalegislature.gov could not be stored: the archiver's connections timed out on 11 and 17 Oct 2026, including a separate attempt for this recheck.

status.quote: Lawmakers approved a measure aimed at creating comprehensive privacy protections for Nebraska agricultural data and strengthening regulation of conversational artificial intelligence.

legal_force.quote: The attorney general is empowered to enforce the provisions through civil action.

summary.quote: The provisions require disclosure when a user reasonably could believe that they are interacting with a human being and add additional safeguards for minor account holders.

The measure also requires a protocol to respond to prompts involving suicidal ideation or self-harm that includes referral to crisis services, and prohibits a service from claiming to be designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care.
The attorney general is empowered to enforce the provisions through civil action.

notes.quote: requires controllers and potential controllers of agricultural data to enter into written consent agreements with agricultural producers before providing, using or selling that data.

Under the bill, starting Jan. 1, 2027, every new contract or agreement involving the collection or processing of agricultural data in Nebraska must include a specific provision that prohibits the selling of that data unless the producer has given express written consent.

judgment.status_reasoning: The stored session review of 15 May 2026 says 'Lawmakers approved a measure ...' and 'LB525 passed on a 49-0 vote', reports no veto, and dates the agricultural contract rule from 1 Jan 2027. It does not give the date of the Governor's signature or the operative date of the AI provisions. The published date_in_force, 1 Jul 2027, is after 18 Oct 2026, so 'Adopted, not yet in force' stands if that date is right; it is left as published, with the dates as open questions.
judgment.scope_reasoning: An AI-specific state act on conversational AI disclosure, minors' safeguards and self-harm protocols, carried in a bill mainly on agricultural data; the AI act itself is clearly in scope, no note (unchanged).
judgment.date_reasoning: No stored file gives date_published or date_in_force; both are left as published and listed as open questions.
